queue.label: Oceanic islands have fewer species than equal continental areas
queue.text: Oceanic islands are inhabited by far fewer species of all kinds than continental areas of equal size, a difference not explained by physical conditions.

queue.label: Plaice weight-length coefficient peaks near the size of sexual maturity
queue.text: In plaice the weight-length coefficient k = W/L^3 is not constant but rises to a maximum and then slowly declines with increasing size, the maximum falling near 30 cm, about the size at which sexual maturity begins.

queue.label: The biconcave red blood corpuscle is not a surface-tension equilibrium figure
queue.text: The biconcave mammalian red blood corpuscle is not a surface of constant mean curvature and so cannot be a fluid drop in equilibrium under surface tension alone; some other force, possibly osmotic inequilibrium or fluid-crystal forces of its cholesterin-like constituents, must maintain its shape, which changes to a sphere in diluted blood.

queue.label: Cannon-bones of ox, sheep and giraffe differ by a simple one-axis stretch
queue.text: The cannon-bones of the ox, sheep and giraffe differ essentially only in relative length and breadth: at equal length, the sheep's bone is about two-thirds and the giraffe's about one-third as broad as the ox's.

queue.label: Changes in the length-weight constant k reveal changes of form during growth
queue.text: Weight varies as the cube of length (W = kL³) in an animal of unchanging form and density, so tracking whether k stays constant or varies with length shows whether the animal's general form changes as it grows; such changes are likely as long as growth continues.

queue.label: Groups rise gradually in species number to a maximum, then gradually decline
queue.text: The number of species in a genus, or genera in a family, generally increases gradually through time to a maximum and then, sooner or later, gradually decreases to extinction.

queue.label: Animals from at most four or five progenitors, plants from as many or fewer
queue.text: All animals have descended from at most four or five progenitors, and all plants from an equal or smaller number.

queue.label: Long ages of abundant life preceded the lowest Silurian strata
queue.text: If descent with modification is true, periods at least as long as the whole time from the Silurian to the present must have passed before the lowest Silurian strata were laid down, and during them the world swarmed with living creatures.

queue.label: Depth expansion and lateral compression vary inversely, conserving fish volume
queue.text: In related fishes, expansion in one transverse dimension tends to be compensated by compression in the other, so that volume at a given length changes less than linear dimensions; the plaice is about twice as deep and half as thick as the haddock and has almost the same length-weight coefficient k = W/L^3.

queue.label: Fine internal networks and granules seen in fixed cells are largely artefacts
queue.text: Fixation preserves the general outward form of small organisms and cells, but the minute internal networks and granules described as the structure of protoplasm are to a large extent artefacts of coagulating fixatives, although larger structures such as nucleus, vacuoles, centrosomes and the spindle are really present in the living cell.

queue.label: Small genera often grow large while large genera peak, decline and vanish
queue.text: Over geological time small genera have often increased greatly in number of species, and large genera have often reached a maximum, declined and disappeared.

queue.label: Close-packed corallites of varying size are on average hexagonal
queue.text: In colonial corals whose corallites are in close contact, the corallites are squeezed into hexagonal prisms; where their sizes vary irregularly they are hexagonal on average, some having fewer and some more than six sides, while loosely bundled corallites stay cylindrical.

queue.label: Small arterial branches leave at large angles, large branches at small angles
queue.text: Small arterial branches come off the main stem at large angles (about 70°–90° for the smallest) and large branches at small angles, with equal branches diverging at equal angles, as Roux's rules state.

queue.label: Species in large genera differ from one another by small amounts
queue.text: In large genera the amount of difference between species is often exceedingly small, so that their species resemble varieties more than do species of small genera.

queue.label: Bivalve growth lines are coaxial curves set by direction-dependent growth rate
queue.text: The lines of growth on bivalve shells are not concentric but coaxial curves through the umbo, and they arise because the rate of growth varies as a simple function of direction; in the simplest case the lines are coaxial circles (as in Anomia), and with more complex functions they are coaxial ellipses or other figures (as in Lima or Solen).

queue.label: A cylindrical cell's end cap has twice the cylinder's radius and height about 0.27R
queue.text: Where a cylindrical cell of uniform wall tension is capped by part of a sphere, the sphere's radius is twice the cylinder's radius, the cap subtends a cone of 60°, and its height is about 0.27 of the cylinder radius (a little more than one-eighth of the diameter), proportions seen in the free end cells of Spirogyra.

queue.label: Higher taxonomic ranks are almost arbitrary
queue.text: The relative value of groups such as orders, sub-orders, families, sub-families and genera is, at least at present, almost arbitrary, as shown by groups being raised in rank merely because more allied species were discovered.

queue.label: Separation or overlap of whorls reflects the growth-rate ratio of outer to inner border
queue.text: Whether the whorls of a spiral shell stand apart, just touch, or overlap (up to complete involution, as in Nautilus pompilius versus N. umbilicatus) depends only on the ratio of the rate of growth of the outer border of the tube to that of its inner border.

queue.label: The scorpioid cyme traces a true logarithmic spiral
queue.text: In a scorpioid cyme, where each shoot arises from the last on the same side at an equal angle and successive shoots diminish in length in a constant ratio, the shoots are tangents to a true logarithmic spiral; in the helicoid cyme the same spiral is present but hidden by a superimposed twist.

queue.label: The smallest organisms approach molecular size, so they cannot be much smaller
queue.text: Because a micrococcus 0.15 µm across contains only some tens of thousands of protein molecules, the smallest known organisms approach molecular dimensions, and organisms cannot be subdivided indefinitely or be much smaller than those already discovered.

queue.label: Most phyllotaxis has between two and three leaves per turn of the genetic spiral
queue.text: The prevalence of Fibonacci parastichy numbers arises because in the great majority of fir-cones and other phyllotactic systems there are more than two but fewer than three leaves in one turn of the genetic spiral (t = 2); other observed series correspond to t = 3, 4, 5.

queue.label: All differences of form between shells are differences of degree in a few growth ratios
queue.text: The form of any turbinate shell is fixed by a small set of factors (shape of the generating curve, its rate of growth, its rate of rotation about the pole, its rate of translation along the axis, and its inclination), and all differences of form between one shell and another are differences of degree in the relative magnitudes of these factors.

queue.label: A cell cutting off under ~3/10 of its volume uses a curved corner wall, not a plane
queue.text: When a cubical or rectangular cell divides unequally and the smaller part is less than about three-tenths of the whole, the minimal partition is a quarter-cylinder cutting off one corner rather than a plane wall; below about 0.15 of the volume a spherical octant in a corner is smaller still.

queue.label: Viscid spider-thread coating breaks into beads at the cylinder stability limit
queue.text: The sticky fluid coating of a spider's spiral thread, being a liquid cylinder, becomes unstable when its length exceeds its circumference and breaks up into equal, equally spaced beads (often with smaller beads between), the spacing being somewhat greater than theory owing to viscosity and drag on the core thread.

queue.label: A quadrant-shaped flat cell divides by a curved anticlinal wall about 3:7 along its side
queue.text: A flattened cell shaped like a quadrant of a circle divides into equal halves by a circular-arc anticlinal wall meeting the side and periphery at right angles, cutting off about 55° 22′ of the arc and starting about three-tenths of the radius from the centre, since this is the shortest bisecting wall.

queue.label: Right-angled cell walls arise because older walls solidify before new partitions form
queue.text: Plant cell walls often meet at right angles (Sachs’s Rule) because an earlier wall has usually become solid and rigid before a later partition joins it, so the fluid partition sets itself at equal angles, i.e. perpendicular, to the rigid wall.

queue.label: Strong cell–cell tension relative to cell–medium tension makes cells round off
queue.text: Where the tension at cell–cell contacts exceeds that at cell–medium surfaces, the external angle between neighbouring cells is less than 120°, and if the cell–cell tension equals or exceeds the sum of the other two the cells touch only at a point, which explains rounded-off blastomeres separated by spaces.

queue.label: Constant growth-rate ratios preserve form; changing ratios produce development
queue.text: When the ratio between growth rates in different directions stays constant, an organism grows in bulk with little or no change of form; such constancy seldom lasts more than a season, and when the ratio alters the organism undergoes development, a steady and persistent change of form.

queue.label: Similarly built animals should jump to the same absolute height regardless of size
queue.text: Because the impulse of a leap is proportional to muscle volume and so to body mass, the take-off velocity is independent of size, and similarly built animals should jump to the same actual height rather than the same relative height; longer levers in larger animals give them some advantage.

queue.label: Cell division restores the ratio of surface to mass
queue.text: Cell division keeps the ratio between a cell's surface and its mass approximately constant and restores the balance of surface energy with the cell's other energies; cleavage of an egg increases surface without increasing volume or mass.

queue.label: Blood-vessels are arranged for minimum effort and minimum wall-surface
queue.text: The form and arrangement of blood-vessels are such that circulation proceeds with a minimum of effort and a minimum of wall-surface (and hence of friction).

queue.label: Shape of paired cells depends on relative tensions at outer surface and partition
queue.text: Whether two adjacent cells in a filament (as in Nostoc and its allies) are separated by flat partitions, are hemispherical, or are each more than a hemisphere depends on the relative magnitudes of the tension at the outer cell surface and at the boundary between the cells.

queue.label: Predation, more often than food supply, sets average numbers
queue.text: Although food sets the upper limit to a species' increase, very often it is destruction by predators rather than food supply that determines the species' average numbers.

queue.label: Differences between varieties grow into differences between species and genera
queue.text: Through natural selection and divergence of character, the small differences between varieties of a species steadily increase until they equal the larger differences between species of the same genus, or even between genera.

queue.label: Each part has its own specific growth rate, on which specific morphology depends
queue.text: A large part of an organism's specific morphology depends on there being, besides an aggregate rate of growth of the whole, a characteristic specific rate of growth for each part or organ, so that small changes in these local rates soon produce striking differences of form.

queue.label: Egg form obeys p_n + T(1/r + 1/r′) = P, the equation of all eggs
queue.text: The shape of an egg, as an extensible membrane filled with incompressible fluid under external pressure, obeys p_n + T(1/r + 1/r′) = P (external normal pressure plus membrane tension times total curvature equals internal pressure), which Thompson calls the equation of all eggs.

queue.label: The number of past intermediate and transitional links was inconceivably great
queue.text: Because all living species are connected through extinct parent-species back to the common ancestor of each great class by steps no greater than those between varieties, the number of intermediate and transitional forms that have lived on earth must have been inconceivably great.

queue.label: Active larvae are adapted to their own conditions as fully as adults
queue.text: Whenever an embryo or larva becomes active and must provide for itself, it is as perfectly adapted to its conditions of life as the adult, and such adaptations can make the larvae of allied species differ as much as or more than their adults, though most larvae still follow the law of embryonic resemblance.

queue.label: Hamilton's rule
queue.text: A gene for social behaviour increases in frequency when the benefit to the recipient, weighted by genetic relatedness, exceeds the cost to the actor.

queue.label: Mean time to fixation of a neutral mutant
queue.text: A neutral mutant that does go to fixation takes on average about four times the effective population size, in generations, to do so.

proposals.reason: No correct Lean statement is writable. The claim (the Glacial period was at least partly simultaneous worldwide) is a dated geological event claim with no quantity to bound or relate; the relation typer labelled it Bound only because of the hedge 'at least'. It stays an empirical claim with its pre-registered test (supports), not a law.

proposals.caveat: The hypothesis family 1 - K^(-a c/s) was not checked against the equations of the 1974 paper; the theorem holds for every K > 1, a > 0.
